$comment: Owner rule R58, runtime proof. User A (walk_organiser) owns the event walk-con-ea5e and the tournaments walk-cup-fee / walk-cup-finished; walk_vendor_bisi owns a stall on that event; walk_buyer_promo holds ticket VT-T6SF8ASW. User B (walk_buyer_ada) is signed in and owns none of it, and every attempt below must be refused with 403 or 404. The records are the walk fixtures on this machine's local sqlite (tools/walk_event.py --setup; password walk-con-2026). Run with the dev server on 8000: node ~/.claude/skills/security-rules/scripts/check-security.mjs --idor http://127.0.0.1:8000. Run --idor BEFORE --live: the live check bursts the login until it sees 429, and the sign-ins here would be caught by that same limiter for the rest of the minute.

cases.name: B cannot read the money on A's event
B cannot pay A's event out
B cannot read A's door list
B cannot read A's promo codes
B cannot add a ticket type to A's event
B cannot read the money on A's tournament
B cannot pay A's tournament out
B cannot read A's tournament staff
B cannot read A's tournament registrations
B cannot read another stallholder's orders
B cannot read the transfer history of somebody else's ticket
B cannot give somebody else's ticket away
